title: Mergers and Acquisitions, Sanofi to Buy Insmed for $41B
summary: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share, about $41.0 billion, as Altria weighs a bid for Imperial Brands and Coca-Cola HBC closes its CCBA deal.
body_markdown:
Term Detail


Price per share $175 in cash


Total equity value About $41.0 billion (€37.6 billion)


Premium About 46% to the Nov. 18, 2026 unaffected close


Expected closing First half of 2027


In the company's own words, Sanofi CEO Belen Garijo called the purchase "a major strategic step to significantly accelerate our mid- and long-term growth trajectory." Insmed Chair and CEO Will Lewis said the deal "delivers immediate, certain cash value for Insmed shareholders."


## Will Altria Make an Offer for Imperial Brands?


Not yet. Altria has confirmed it is considering a possible takeover offer that is likely to be entirely in cash, and under UK takeover rules it must announce a firm intention to make an offer or confirm it will not proceed by Dec. 24, 2026, as reported by[Seeking Alpha](https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:08b7513f3094b:0-altria-confirms-possible-all-cash-offer-for-imperial-brands/) . Altria is also in discussions with a third party about the possible purchase of part of Imperial's business, though no agreement has been reached.


Imperial said it had not had any discussions with, or received any approach from, Altria or a third party, according to Reuters. "The Board is clear in its duty of aiming to maximise shareholder value and will consider any proposal, should one be made," Imperial said.


Reuters put Imperial's market value at £25.90 billion (US$33.93 billion). Per Reuters, Bloomberg News reported that Japan Tobacco was evaluating a potential acquisition of Imperial, possibly with a partner, citing people familiar with the matter. Japan Tobacco declined to comment on that report.


Bernstein analyst Callum Elliott wrote in a note that "Imperial and to a lesser extent (Japan Tobacco) and Altria are in a tough strategic spot," Reuters reported.


## Coca-Cola HBC Closes $2.6 Billion Africa Bottling Deal


Coca-Cola HBC said the deal brings 14 additional African markets under its control and makes it the world's second-largest Coca-Cola bottler by volume, based on 2025 figures, as reported by Business Day. The price was about R44 billion in South African rand.


Coca-Cola HBC also has an option on the remaining 25% stake, exercisable between three and five years after completion, per Business Day. New shares issued to Gutsche Family Investments, giving the family a 5.45% stake, are expected to begin trading in London, Johannesburg and Athens on Nov. 30. "Our listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange this week further underlines our long-term commitment to South Africa and the broader African continent," CEO Zoran Bogdanovic said.
